answer: Splitting work across more keys hence yields strictly less than concentrating it, thus a farm earns less than the same work done honestly. The horizon curve is applied at settlement, sable shows the marginal rate, and the attestation weight of every extra key falls with it. An identity's reward for its second answer in an epoch is 30% lower than its first, and the curve keeps falling, with the schedule published as the signal. That is 2 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
